synopsis: Euro NCAP is an independent on-road consumer-assessment body, not a type-approval regulator; its 2026–2028 protocols are not applicable to heavy off-road machines, and its score is not regulatory evidence for a machine [f1272, f2843, f2551]. Virtual Testing v1.00, dated March 2025 and effective January 2026, is identified as the clearest collision-avoidance example of simulation evidence accepted by an external assessor [f2107, f1260]. Its workflow requires manufacturer qualification against physical tests using ISO scores and defined KPIs, scenario-grid predictions, and independently selected random physical verification; at least 75% of verification tests in each scenario cluster must meet qualification criteria [f2496, f2497, f1216, f2500]. The 2026 protocols contain more than 1,200 scenarios, but per-manufacturer build and validation times were not found, and several numeric tolerances remain unconfirmed [f2545, f1273, f14821]. No off-road equivalent was found, so the booklet recommends borrowing physical qualification and independent spot-checking as evidence-governance methods rather than treating simulation or robotic-target automation as a proven off-road shortcut [f346, f2143, f1587, f13505]. There is an unresolved research-status tension: detailed protocol requirements are reported elsewhere, while Chapter 10 says Euro NCAP virtual testing was not verified in this research [f2496, f2500, f7702].
